domain.name: Music & Audio Production
domain.description: Practical recording, editing, arrangement, beat production, sound design, mixing, mastering, and delivery fundamentals.

competencies.name: Recording & Signal Flow
competencies.description: Capture clean audio using appropriate gain structure, routing, monitoring, and room awareness.
competencies.purpose: Prevent avoidable recording defects before post-production.

units.title: Good capture protects every later stage
units.content: Mic choice, placement, room sound, gain, monitoring, and performance quality usually matter more than trying to repair severe capture problems later.

units.title: Recording setup
units.content: Choose source and mic/DI path; set position; check cable and routing; set gain with headroom; monitor for noise, clipping, latency, and room issues; record a test; then lock the setup before takes.

units.title: Recording failures
units.content: Avoid clipping, recording too quietly without reason, monitoring only after the session, ignoring room reflections, and changing setup between takes without documentation.

drills.title: Build a vocal recording setup
drills.prompt: Design a vocal recording setup for a small untreated room, including mic placement, gain, monitoring, room control, and test procedure.

competencies.name: Vocal Editing
competencies.description: Comp, clean, tune, time-align, and prepare vocals while preserving performance character.
competencies.purpose: Create polished vocals without over-processing expression.

units.title: Vocal edit order
units.content: Comp for performance first; clean obvious noise and clicks; align timing only where needed; correct pitch transparently to the song style; manage breaths and transitions; then render or consolidate cleanly before mix processing.

units.title: Edit toward intention, not mechanical perfection
units.content: Small timing and pitch variations often carry feel; correct what distracts from the song rather than flattening every human variation.

units.title: Vocal edit failures
units.content: Avoid tuning before choosing the best take, cutting natural phrase transitions, deleting every breath, over-aligning doubles, and hiding bad edits under heavy effects.

drills.title: Plan a lead vocal comp
drills.prompt: Given five takes with different strengths, explain how to choose phrases, smooth edits, and decide where pitch or timing correction is justified.

competencies.name: Beat Production & Arrangement
competencies.description: Develop rhythm, harmony, texture, and section structure into a complete instrumental.
competencies.purpose: Turn loops and ideas into songs with movement and contrast.

units.title: Arrangement manages energy and expectation
units.content: Sections feel different through density, register, rhythm, silence, automation, and sound changes; adding tracks is only one way to create movement.

units.title: From loop to full arrangement
units.content: Identify the core musical idea; establish intro, verse, hook, bridge or transition roles as needed; create energy changes; remove competing elements; automate transitions; then test whether the song stays engaging without visual cues.

units.title: Arrangement failures
units.content: Avoid eight-bar loops with no development, every section using the same density, transitions that rely only on risers, and adding parts that compete with the vocal space.

drills.title: Turn a loop into a song
drills.prompt: Take a strong eight-bar loop and design a three-minute arrangement with distinct verse, hook, transitions, and one contrast section.

competencies.name: Sound Design & Sampling
competencies.description: Shape and transform audio using synthesis, sampling, layering, envelopes, filtering, and modulation.
competencies.purpose: Create distinctive sounds while maintaining musical function and lawful source use.

units.title: Sound design starts with role
units.content: A sound should serve rhythm, harmony, texture, impact, or atmosphere; complexity without a role can make a mix harder rather than better.

units.title: Layered sound design
units.content: Define the sound's job; choose a strong base source; shape envelope and tone; add only complementary layers; control frequency overlap; add motion; then test in the mix rather than solo.

units.title: Sound-design failures
units.content: Avoid stacking multiple similar layers for loudness, ignoring sample rights, designing only in solo, and using effects that destroy transient or pitch clarity needed by the role.

drills.title: Design a signature transition hit
drills.prompt: Build a transition impact from layered legal sources while assigning each layer a distinct frequency or texture role.

competencies.name: Mixing: Balance, Space & Tone
competencies.description: Create a coherent mix through level, pan, EQ, dynamics, space, and automation.
competencies.purpose: Make important elements clear and emotionally effective across playback systems.

units.title: Mix priority workflow
units.content: Start with arrangement and static balance; identify focal elements; solve masking with level and arrangement before heavy processing; use EQ and dynamics for specific problems; create depth with ambience; automate changes across sections; then reference at matched loudness.

units.title: Balance before plugins
units.content: If the song does not communicate with faders and basic panning, more processing often hides rather than solves the core problem.

units.title: Mix failures
units.content: Avoid boosting every track for clarity, compressing by habit, widening low-frequency content carelessly, mixing only loud, and referencing at unequal loudness.

drills.title: Mix around a lead vocal
drills.prompt: Describe how to create space for a lead vocal in a dense beat using arrangement, levels, EQ, dynamics, ambience, and automation.

competencies.name: Dynamics & Loudness Control
competencies.description: Use compression, limiting, transient control, and gain staging without destroying musical movement.
competencies.purpose: Control peaks and density while preserving impact.

units.title: Loudness and dynamics are tradeoffs
units.content: Higher average loudness can reduce transient contrast and movement; the target should fit the release context rather than chasing the highest possible level.

units.title: Dynamics decision workflow
units.content: Identify whether the problem is peak, consistency, envelope, sustain, or loudness; choose the appropriate tool; set thresholds and timing by listening; level-match bypass; then verify the result in context.

units.title: Dynamics failures
units.content: Avoid compressing because a track looks dynamic, judging processors louder-vs-quieter, brickwalling early in the mix, and using fast attack settings that erase needed transients.

drills.title: Control drum dynamics
drills.prompt: Choose processing for a drum bus that has strong peaks but loses punch when compressed heavily.

competencies.name: Mastering & Release Delivery
competencies.description: Prepare final mixes for consistent translation, loudness, sequencing, metadata, and file delivery.
competencies.purpose: Create release-ready masters without masking mix problems.

units.title: Mastering review
units.content: Confirm final mix quality and headroom; compare references at matched loudness; make broad corrective moves only when needed; control peaks and final level; check mono and multiple playback systems; export required formats; verify metadata and files.

units.title: Mastering should not rescue a broken mix
units.content: When a problem is isolated to one element or arrangement choice, fix the mix when possible instead of forcing the stereo master to compensate.

units.title: Mastering failures
units.content: Avoid clipping inter-sample peaks, over-brightening for perceived detail, excessive limiting, exporting only one archival format, and skipping final file verification.

drills.title: Prepare a single for release
drills.prompt: Create a mastering and delivery checklist for a streaming single including references, loudness judgment, peak control, formats, metadata, and QC.

competencies.name: Session & File Management
competencies.description: Organize sessions, versions, stems, backups, and deliverables so projects remain recoverable.
competencies.purpose: Protect creative work and speed collaboration.

units.title: Audio project organization
units.content: Use consistent session naming; keep source audio, edits, prints, stems, and masters in defined locations; save milestone versions; consolidate external files; maintain at least one independent backup; document final deliverables.

units.title: A session is not safe because it opens today
units.content: Recovery depends on copied assets, version history, plugin dependencies, and backups, not only the project file.

units.title: Session-management failures
units.content: Avoid destructive overwrites, missing external samples, final_v7_REAL naming chaos, exporting stems with inconsistent start points, and storing the only copy on one drive.

drills.title: Design an album session structure
drills.prompt: Create naming, versioning, stem, backup, and master-delivery rules for a multi-song project.
